Amy (Sales): Heads-up — Orchid Health is asking if an air-gapped on‑prem POC is feasible. Key asks: signed bundles, SBOM, HSM integration, offline activation, and a constrained upgrade cadence (they want major upgrades every ~2 years). Can we confirm constraints and rough pricing? Meeting Fri 10am.
Alex R: Short answer: doable, but a few tradeoffs. We can produce signed, chunked bundles + SBOM and support PKCS#11 HSM flows. Offline activation token per-node is supported. Major upgrades every 2 years OK, but we'd push quarterly security delta patches for CVEs; otherwise risk grows.
Maria L: Ops notes — for airgap we recommend delta-chunking to reduce transfer size. Typical bundle: base image + quantized model tar (~1.8GB for int8) + runtime (~300MB). Deltas between releases are usually <50MB if we split model weights and container layers.
Jordan (Sec): Security checklist highlights: FIPS / gov PKI requirement, signed SBOM (CycloneDX), reproducible build proof, chain-of-custody docs, and HSM key-import audit trail. Need to confirm third-party deps license list. Also ask legal about indemnity on model weights.
Sam T: Pricing question — do we invoice per-node for Private installs or can we offer reserved capacity-like pricing for a larger onprem fleet? Also POC discounts?
Alex R: For Private/on‑prem we typically do term-based per-node licenses. For POCs we can do a short pilot license (e.g., up to 5 nodes free / deeply discounted for 30–60 days). For enterprise customers we can negotiate commit pricing that mimics Dedicated (monthly commit) but applied to node counts.
Amy (Sales): Great. Can eng/ops draft a one‑page POC tech summary + a short pricing template I can hand to their procurement? Also we need a simple runbook for offline activation steps for their ops team.
Maria L: I'll draft runbook: include offline activation CLI + jumpbox workflow. Example verification command we use for customers:

openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz

And an offline install step snippet:

1) transfer chunks via secure USB or jumpbox
2) on target: cat chunk.* | tar -xz -C /opt/redwood
3) ./redwoodctl activate --token <token> --node-id <id>

Jordan (Sec): Also require SBOM + signed hash file and a short attestation template for chain-of-custody. I'll assemble checklist and share here.
deploy-bot: build artifact b-20240822-001 signed (sha256: c3f5...) uploaded to internal-artifacts (timestamp 2024-08-22T15:02:03Z)
Sam T: For the SOW I'll propose: pilot: 5 nodes, 30 days, standard support; pilot price if they need >5 nodes: $X/node/month or convert to committed nodes on contract. Will confirm number with finance.
Amy (Sales): Perfect. Action items: @Jordan produce security checklist, @Maria produce runbook + bundle size estimates, @Alex confirm HSM PKCS#11 integration notes for their HSM vendor (Thales/YubiHSM etc.). I'll reply to customer with tentative plan and propose Fri 10am call.
Jordan (Sec): Will post checklist by EOD. Any high-risk blockers I should flag now?
Alex R: Only blocker is if their ops team forbids any quarterly patches — we should push for at least CVE hotfix cadence. Also need to confirm allowed transport method (USB vs approved jumpbox). If they limit to USB only, we need chain-of-custody + signed chunk-level verification stricter.
Amy (Sales): Noted. Thanks team — I'll sync with Orchid and schedule the call. :thumbsup:
